key_insight: AutoResearch uses an LLM as an offline research agent to autonomously tune aerospace control policies, while an embedded credibility layer audits each claimed improvement against seed noise and ablation checks.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reproducible way to develop and verify spacecraft guidance, navigation, and control policies so that only statistically credible gains are promoted for deployment.
method: LLM reads a plain-language problem description plus run history and proposes one training-script edit per iteration.
Each candidate result is validated by measured per-problem seed noise, reseeded verification of the best configuration, and leave-one-out pruning of agent edits.
The same audited loop is applied to two spacecraft control tasks: relative rendezvous and safety-constrained docking past a keep-out zone.
evidence_signal: Across both benchmark problems, the audited policy exceeds measured seed noise by many standard deviations; on docking, the learned policy remains outside the keep-out zone on every seed while undirected search finds no feasible policy.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on problem-specific seed-noise calibration and repeated verification, its credibility depends on carefully designed benchmarks and sufficient compute for repeated runs.
paper_title: Agentic AutoResearch forSpace Autonomy: An Auditable, LLM-Driven Research Agent for Aerospace Control Problems
